subject: Next steps: account erase kickoff, KMS handoff, and snapshot constraints
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Harris <michael.harris@finplatform.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-18T15:05:00Z
Subject: Follow-up & proposed erase kickoff timeline

Hi Michael — great to speak earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side for the account erase/RTBF scope you described: 

- Scope we captured: user PII (name, email), model interaction logs, embeddings for support transcripts. You indicated retention rules for analytics (90 days) and a stricter requirement to purge PII within 30 days for terminated accounts.
- Proposed Redwood approach:
  * Immediate: create a scoped erase runbook for your account (we'll map object keys + retention buckets).
  * KMS/key policy: handoff plan to rotate customer-managed key on purge day so tokens stored encrypted with customer key are irrecoverable.
  * Backups: we noted you have immutable snapshots on your side — we recommend a backup purge window and exception workflow.

Can you confirm the 30-day hard-delete SLA for PII and which backup systems are considered immutable? If confirmed, we can schedule a kickoff with engineering to map the endpoints and confirm any required contract addendum.

Attachments: FinPlatform_Retention_Requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet we referred to on the call)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Michael Harris <michael.harris@finplatform.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: FinPlatform Security <security@finplatform.com>
Date: 2025-11-18T17:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed erase kickoff timeline

Ben/Rachel — thanks for the recap. Confirming:

- Yes, PII must be purged within 30 calendar days from the deletion request for terminated users.
- Analytics buckets (aggregated events) may persist up to 90 days; embeddings used for search must be deleted with PII.
- Backup situation: our long-term snapshots (on our object store) are immutable for 120 days due to audit controls. We need to understand how Redwood's purge pipeline handles these snapshots and whether you can provide attestation once the in-prod data is removed.

I’ve looped in our security team (security@finplatform.com) — they’ll share our data retention annex and an initial list of snapshot object prefixes. Attaching the retention spreadsheet you mentioned.

-Michael
Michael Harris
Head of Platform Security, FinPlatform
michael.harris@finplatform.com

Attachment: FinPlatform_Retention_Requirements.xlsx

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: FinPlatform Security <security@finplatform.com>, Michael Harris <michael.harris@finplatform.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-19T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed erase kickoff timeline

Michael / Security team — thanks for confirming. Looping in Soojin (Privacy Ops) and Marissa (Customer Reliability) so we can align on both the technical and evidence/attestation pieces.

High-level plan we propose (requested confirmations in bold):

1) Scope & object mapping (this week)
   - Soojin will run a quick discovery to map which keys correspond to "PII" vs "analytics". Please share the snapshot prefixes when convenient. **Action: security@finplatform.com to share list by EOD Wednesday.**

2) KMS handoff & key rotation (erase event)
   - Options: (A) Redwood rotates a customer-managed key in the KMS and triggers an immediate rewrap/purge; (B) Customer performs a rotate+revoke and provides proof-of-rotation. We prefer (A) for an auditable, single-step workflow. **Action: Michael — which option do you prefer?**

3) Backups & immutable snapshots
   - Important constraint: if a snapshot is genuinely immutable for 120 days on your object store, Redwood cannot directly delete objects you control. We can:
     a) Provide a documented attestation (time-stamped report) when in-prod data and our own retained copies are removed; and
     b) Offer an optional remediation script/manifest you can run to scrub prefixes in your snapshot store once policy permits.
   - **Please confirm which vendor/store hosts the immutable snapshots and whether FinPlatform accepts attestation + a later manual purge.**

4) Evidence and audit artifacts
   - We can supply: deletion runbook, a deletion manifest (keys removed), KMS rotation logs, and a signed attestation PDF. If you require SOC2 incremental evidence, we can coordinate an evidence package with our compliance team.

5) Timeline suggestion
   - Discovery/Mapping: 3 business days after snapshot prefixes received
   - Implementation/Testing: 5 business days
   - Production erase run: target within 30 days from customer request (per your SLA) — final date to be agreed after mapping.

Next steps: Michael/security team — share snapshot prefixes and confirm KMS option (A or B). We’ll prepare a scoped erase matrix and a short DocuSign addendum if needed.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Dir, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Harris <michael.harris@finplatform.com>, FinPlatform Security <security@finplatform.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-20T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed erase kickoff timeline

Michael / security team — putting the operational summary in one place for the kickoff call: 

- We will deliver a scoped erase matrix (CSV) that maps Redwood object keys to your retention buckets. Expect the CSV via HubSpot link within 48 hours.
- For immutable snapshots: Redwood will provide an attestation artifact and a manifest for your team to run to erase snapshot prefixes once your immutable window closes. We will not delete objects in customer-managed snapshot stores without explicit authorization.
- KMS: we recommend option (A) — Redwood triggers a rotation+revocation event under a customer-managed key policy to produce a single-step irrecoverable state for our copies. If you prefer option (B) we’ll accept proof of rotation and a signed revocation event.
- Evidence: deletion manifest, KMS rotation log, and signed attestation PDF; DocuSign addendum will only be used if legal requires express wording around backups.

Action items we will execute this week:
- Whiteboard session with your engineers to map endpoints (schedule — please propose two 60-min slots)
- Prepare the erase matrix (we’ll upload to the HubSpot deal record)
- Draft a short evidence checklist for your auditors (SOC2-ready)

Thanks and looking forward to the kickoff — Marissa will schedule the call after you provide snapshot prefixes.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: scoped-erase-matrix.csv
